Date: 2025-07-19T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Live streaming latency impacting conversational sessions - BrightMerchant

Hi Samira,

We detected elevated end-to-end latency on our streaming/chat endpoints that could be affecting live conversational sessions for BrightMerchant between 08:50–09:10 PDT. Metrics show token emission delays and sporadic chunking in the response stream. Our SREs have started an investigation and we've opened an incident (INC-2124).

Immediate notes and asks:
- We've enabled additional telemetry capture for your account and raised sampling for streaming traces.
- Could you confirm whether you observed similar delays on your side and, if possible, share a recent session ID or request IDs (x-request-id) so we can correlate?
- Temporary mitigations we recommend: lower per-request max_tokens to 512, switch to the non-streaming fallback for critical low-latency flows, and add a 1500ms client-side reconnect backoff for streaming sessions.

I'll keep you updated hourly; Ben is leading the triage. Apologies for the disruption — we're prioritizing minimizing impact while we identify root cause.

Best,
Irene Choi
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Hi Irene — thanks for the heads up. We did see a spike on our side around 08:55 where agent replies were delayed by several seconds and a few sessions dropped the stream and fell back to polling.

Request IDs we pulled from our logs: rwb-44b2, rwb-44b8, rwb-44c1. I've attached a small export of one session timeline (attached: bm_session_sample.json) and a pcap snippet Derek grabbed during the spike.

—Samira

Forwarding Samira's note and attachments. Early triage summary below.

On Jul 19, 2025, Samira Khan <samira.k@brightmerchant.com> wrote:
> Hi Irene — thanks for the heads up. We did see a spike on our side around 08:55 ...

Triage notes (SRE):
- We saw increased queuing on several edge workers in us-west-2 between 08:50–09:05. CPU and GPU utilization were normal; latency correlated with a congestion event on the streaming ingress layer.
- A subset of streaming worker processes reported elevated event-loop stalls while applying prefix caching logic; disabling the prefix-cache hot-path reduced emission latency in the canary pool.
- Kept live instrumentation enabled; we've collected kv-cache metrics, per-request kernel timings, and packet captures.

Immediate actions taken:
1) Scoped traffic away from impacted ingress pool; routed BrightMerchant to a warm standby pool (should reduce new requests queueing).
2) Disabled prefix-cache hot-path for a short window in the canary — confirmed emission latency improved by ~60% in synthetic tests.
3) Collected traces and a pcap that I've uploaded to the incident page.

Next steps:
- Complete analysis of the prefix-cache regression and roll a targeted fix (low-risk code path change).
- Prepare a short postmortem for BrightMerchant with timeline, root cause, and recommended mitigations.
- Offer a one-time credit for customer impact (coordinate with Rishi for commercial).

Assigning action items:
- Marissa: coordinate customer comms and finalize the postmortem draft.
- Logan: correlate x-request-ids and produce a per-request timeline (deliverable by EOD).
- Rishi: prepare a proposed goodwill credit and escalation plan.

Ben
Staff SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@brightmerchant.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-07-23T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Post-incident summary & remediation steps — BrightMerchant streaming latency (INC-2124)

Hi Samira and team,

TL;DR — We identified a regression in the prefix-cache hot-path in our streaming runtime that caused intermittent event-loop stalls under a particular request shape and burst pattern. We mitigated the impact on Jul 19 by routing BrightMerchant traffic to a warm standby pool and applying a temporary toggle to bypass the hot-path. End-to-end emission latency returned to normal within ~20 minutes for routed requests.

What happened (timeline):
- 08:48 PDT: automated alert — increased p50/p95 emission lag for streaming endpoints serving BrightMerchant.
- 08:50–09:05 PDT: queuing spikes on a subset of ingress workers; customers experienced delayed token emission and a small number of session disconnects.
- 09:00 PDT: SRE canary tests reproduced the delay when prefix-cache hot-path was enabled.
- 09:10 PDT: traffic rerouted and prefix-cache hot-path disabled in canary; improvements observed.
- 09:25 PDT: mitigation rolled to affected pool; streaming performance normalized for most sessions.

Root cause:
- A recent optimization for prefix caching introduced a contention point that under certain burst patterns caused event-loop stalls while materializing cached prefixes. This was not triggered in our standard synthetic testbeds which used a different request distribution.

Customer impact:
- BrightMerchant saw increased p95 latency and a small fraction (<0.6%) of streaming sessions that fell back to polling for subsequent tokens during the 08:50–09:10 window.

Remediation and long-term fixes: 
1) Patch the prefix-cache materialization to be non-blocking (in progress; targeted rollback-safe patch scheduled for 2025-07-25).
2) Expand synthetic test shard to include more bursty request patterns and larger prefix sizes.
3) Add an automatic failover threshold that will reroute traffic to standby pools if ingress queue depth exceeds safe thresholds for more than 30s.

Short-term customer guidance (what you can do now):
- If you see a future spike, reducing per-request max_tokens to 512 helps reduce serialization overhead.
- Implement a 1500ms reconnect backoff for streaming clients; our SDKs will default to this after the patch.
- Consider enabling client-side jitter when reconnecting to avoid synchronized reconnect storms.

Attachments: redwood-postmortem-draft.pdf (postmortem draft), bm_latency_logs_20250719.zip (collected traces), stream-pcap-20250719.txt (pcap extract).

Commercial goodwill: Rishi will follow up with a proposed one-time credit; we want to ensure the remediation is effective before finalizing amounts.

Open action items for BrightMerchant:
- Share any additional x-request-ids you find from 08:45–09:15 so Logan can correlate server traces.
- Let us know a convenient time for a 30-minute post-incident review call next week.

Apologies again for the disruption — we're committed to preventing recurrence and will share the final postmortem after the patch lands.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
